1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.d4 Nxe4 4.Bd3 d5 5.N.strategy: Retakes the pawn, restoring material equality and centralising the knight, which the d-pawn defends. Black can no longer drive it away with ...d6, since the pawn already stands on d5, so Black has to challenge it by other means. The position is symmetrical and level, with White's knight the more active piece.

Challenges the knight on e5 at once and develops the bishop for castling, keeping the position fully symmetrical. A solid choice that was once a main reply and is now played less often than the alternatives.
